Solve the supplied rule-constrained task. Return short JSON matching the response schema. Jointly propose an executable rule sketch and any entity/group/usage interface. Do not omit exceptions. A compiled unit needs a source link to a binding or query; unlisted units remain residual. Do not claim unsupported text is compiled. program.kind is expression, connector, or unsupported. For expression body use bindings [{name,value,type,source}], query {op,args}, source_links {unit:[node]}. Types: integer, rational (decimal string), scalar. Connectors also accept relation A string input uses type scalar, not string. Expression names start with n_ for numbers, s_ for strings, b_ for booleans; source IDs such as s0 are provenance only. An expression body requires bindings, query and source_links. Do not copy every source sentence into bindings; bind only public literals needed by an executable query. If no faithful query is available, use unsupported with body {} and keep the native answer separate. {columns,rows,closed}, amount (one value,unit,owner,period,lineage,stage object), amounts (a list of these objects), allowance_bank (entries key,balance,policy,order_observable), resource_key, slot_list. Do not invent entity witnesses or guess allocation policies. A variable is {var:name}. Operators: if,and,or,not,eq,ne,lt,le,add,sub,min,max,scale (literal constant first), divide_constant (literal denominator), array,pair,object,concat. No arbitrary code. Bind observed values and rule constants from public source units. Node names are query and binding:NAME. Use unsupported with empty body when faithful executable translation is unavailable. Always give your task answer in answer; this fixed fallback has no stability certificate. Interface proposals may describe a source-linked join/group/map/reduce graph, but never use source IDs or answers as routing features. Each interfaces entry has exactly fields (allowed semantic field names), graph (connector DSL), and bindings (same source-linked binding format); use [] when unavailable. A connector body has bindings,candidates,source_links,project; optional query wraps its result. Projection modes: identity, amount_value (one Amount), amount_values (list of Amount), entailment_label (Boolean claim to binary Entailment/Contradiction). A wrapper query reads n_result/b_result/s_result, or n_result_0,n_result_1,... for numeric list results. Never bind these output names as public inputs. An expression variable may remain unbound only if public text itself declares its full finite domain: Boolean b_NAME = true/false.; Integer n_NAME in [integers] = integer.; or Enum s_NAME in [strings] = string. Keep its untranslated source unit residual. Other unread text has unknown scope; do not invent domains or missing rules. Do not store case amounts or names as reusable skill constants. Answer contract: integer total cost
Executable contract clarification: bindings contain only extracted public inputs and rule constants; never put an answer object or a program into a scalar string. JSON text in a string is not executable. A source identifier such as s0 is provenance metadata, never a boolean or a variable. Read a bound input with {"var":"name"}. and/or/not take booleans; comparisons return booleans. Expression binding names use n_ for integer/rational, s_ for strings, b_ for booleans; numeric references must name n_ slots, string keys s_ slots, boolean references b_ slots. Choose op before writing args. The maximum expression depth is16; use concise expressions. The root query must return the native task result: a numeric operation for Airline, an if producing an Entailment/Contradiction string for SARA, and an object operation producing EC/EV for OpenExempt. OpenExempt EC values are arrays of literal legal citation strings containing §. EV values are arrays of object operations with exactly citation (a literal citation string) and claim_value (a numeric expression). if has exactly [boolean condition, complete true branch, complete false branch]; both branches must type check. add/sub/min/max/lt/le take exact numbers. scale is [literal integer, numeric expression]; divide_constant is [numeric expression, nonzero literal integer]. Arrays use {op:array,args:[...]}; pair is [string key,value expression]; object takes pair operations as its args, never raw JSON fields. source_links maps current unit IDs to existing node names: query or binding:NAME (connector:i for connectors). Use actual cited lines for each input; cite all rule/exception lines needed for the query. Every scalar string must be an exact nonempty substring of its cited unit, never a paraphrase. A boolean binding is allowed only when its cited unit explicitly contains the standalone literal true or false. Assumptions, inferred states and absent information are not boolean inputs. Express rule conditions using comparisons on quoted inputs; otherwise leave the translation unsupported. Do not mark unrelated units compiled. Omitted units remain residual. Unknown semantics must remain unsupported, never replaced with a guessed rule. Interfaces use only the seven documented connector operators, or []. The complete example below illustrates syntax using an invented task. Its answer definition and facts belong only to that invented task. Read the CURRENT public question to determine all required components of its answer. Compile the current public task afresh.
[{"public_text":"Number of parcels: 2.\nFee per parcel is 7; multiply the count by 7.","proposal":{"program":{"kind":"expression","body":{"bindings":[{"name":"n_count","type":"integer","value":2,"source":"s0"},{"name":"n_fee","type":"integer","value":7,"source":"s1"}],"query":{"op":"scale","args":[7,{"var":"n_count"}]},"source_links":{"s0":["query"],"s1":["query"]}}},"answer":14,"compiled_units":["s0","s1"],"unsupported_units":[],"interfaces":[]}}]
The original Airline task asks for the total travel cost, including the supplied flight ticket and all applicable checked baggage fees. The invented syntax example does not redefine this task.

[s0] # Bag fees
[s1] All published bag fees apply at each check-in location and are base rates according to travel dates and destination; applicable taxes are not shown.
[s2] ## Carry-on bags
[s3] You're allowed 1 carry-on bag and 1 personal item in all cabins.
[s4] ### Personal items
[s5] Your personal item like a purse or small handbag must fit under the seat in front of you. Dimensions should not exceed 18 x 14 x 8 inches (45 x 35 x 20 cm).
[s6] These don't count as your personal item or carry-on:
[s7] * Diaper bags (1 per child)
[s8] * Breast pump
[s9] * Small, soft-sided cooler of breast milk
[s10] * Child safety seats, strollers and medical or mobility devices
[s11] ### Carry-on items
[s12] You can bring only one carry-on item along with your personal item. Your carry-on must fit in in the overhead bin or under the seat in front of you. If it doesn't fit, it will need to be checked. Be sure all your carry-on items are labeled in case they are checked.
[s13] #### Carry-on bag
[s14] The total size of your carry-on, including the handles and wheels, cannot exceed 22 x 14 x 9 inches (56 x 36 x 23 cm) and must fit in the sizer at the airport.
[s15] #### Soft-sided garment bag
[s16] Your soft-sided garment bag cannot exceed 51 inches / 130 cm (length + width + height).
[s17] ## Checked bags
[s18] Bag fees have been updated effective for tickets issued on / after February 20, 2024.
[s19] Travel within / between the U.S., Puerto Rico, and U.S. Virgin Islands – 1st checked bag fee is $40 and the 2nd checked bag fee is $45.
[s20] Travel to / from Canada, Caribbean, Mexico, Central America, and Guyana – 1st checked bag fee is $35 and the 2nd checked bag fee is $45.
[s21] All bag fees are non-refundable and apply per person, each way, even if you buy or get an upgrade that includes free checked bags. If you believe you were incorrectly charged for bag fees, contact an American representative for help or file a refund claim within 45 days.
